Decision: keep full tech-stack + data-folder disclosure on About. Reasoning: Vanish has zero network I/O (asserted by test/network-verify.ps1), so exact Electron/Chromium/Node versions and the local data-folder path are never exposed to anyone but the person already sitting at the machine looking at its own About panel - there is no remote attacker this could inform. Matches the project's stated transparency ethos ('never pretends it can do something it cannot'). Not changed: the data-folder line could become a clickable 'reveal in Explorer' action to match Settings' existing set-open-data button, but that is a UX nicety, not a disclosure-risk fix - left for a future pass, not bundled into this one.

That gap, not an Audit-Mode write block (set-settings is NOT fullModeOnly-gated - checked main.js:705), was the real mechanism: any real latency in writeSettings' disk I/O could catch a screenshot mid-gap with the toggle already ON next to the OFF-state text. Wording also restated (ON/OFF prefix) so the two can't be misread as describing different states even without the race. npm test 371/0 unaffected (Settings validation suite covers this path unelevated); not interactively re-clicked in a live window from this session.

scanner.ps1 Get-NetConnectionsByProcess now returns entry.peers.Keys (the IP list, already being collected) instead of discarding it after Count. Renderer renders an expandable per-row peer-IP list (net-peers-toggle/net-peers-list). No port, no DNS - both limits kept exactly as before.

renderNetworkHold now lists each held BITS jobs displayName (state.record.bitsJobs, already captured by network-hold-capture, only its Count was ever shown) instead of just a number. True PID-level attribution isnt possible - Get-BitsTransfer exposes no owning-process field - so this is the concrete-but-honest version: name the actual transfers, not a guessed process correlation.

redundancyWaivers array added to settings.json (lib/store.js, reuses existing get-settings/set-settings IPC - no new store file, no new IPC handler). renderRedundancyGroups (renderer.js) now renders a per-app Review-to-uninstall button (jumps to All Apps tab, clears filters, calls the same selectApp() a manual click would, stops short of auto-opening the wizard since the redundancy apps object is a collapsed family summary not necessarily the live registry row) and a per-group Keep-all-of-these/waive toggle. scanner.ps1 Get-GpuUsageByProcess (Get-Counter GPU Engine Utilization Percentage, same source Windows Task Manager itself uses) added as its own IPC action (get-gpu-usage), deliberately separate from list-processes. Measured live on the operators actual machine: 1.5-3.2s per call, so the renderer samples it on its own 15s interval (GPU_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_MS), not the fast 1-60s-configurable process-list tick - merged into the table client-side by pid. New GPU column + sort key in Task Manager. System-wide GPU-0/GPU-1 activity pills above the table (generic phys-index labels, not a guessed vendor name - matches real Task Managers own precedent for the identical limitation). Verified end to end against the real dual-GPU machine (AMD iGPU + RTX 3080), confirmed correct parsing of live instance names.

Root cause confirmed via a clean, single-script live timing test (launch to real main window, both same methodology, both under the operators actual startupMode=full auto-elevate path): NSIS-installed build 4165ms, portable exe 20433ms - a ~5x difference. This isolates the portable packaging format (self-extraction to a fresh TEMP folder on every launch, likely compounded by real-time antivirus scanning the newly-extracted files - Kaspersky avp.exe confirmed active on this machine) as the dominant cause of the reported 5-8s+ startup wait, not app code. No further code fix exists on the Vanish side - this is inherent to the portable packaging format. Recommendation for the operator: default to the NSIS-installed build for regular use; keep portable for no-install/USB scenarios where the tradeoff is accepted.

Resolved via a different, more reliable path than the blocked DXGI COM interop attempt: Electron already enumerates every GPU adapter internally for its own rendering (app.getGPUInfo(complete)) and exposes vendorId + deviceString + active per adapter - live-tested and confirmed correct vendor IDs (0x1002=AMD, 0x10DE=NVIDIA) for both real GPUs on the operators machine, no custom native interop needed at all. New get-gpu-vendors IPC handler (main.js) wraps this, filtered to exclude the Microsoft Basic Render Driver software fallback. Real AMD/NVIDIA logos added to assets/icons.css (fa-amd, fa-nvidia) sourced from Simple Icons (CC0-licensed icon files; the marks themselves remain their respective trademark owners, informational hardware-identification use). Correlation to the GPU Engine perf counters phys_N index is still array-order best-effort (no LUID exposed by getGPUInfo to prove it definitively) - the numeric GPU 0/GPU 1 label stays alongside the logo for exactly this reason, documented in code comments. npm test 371/0, npm run verify 174/0, icon-verify 3/0 - all clean.

Confirmed via the real Steam registry key: Steam DOES still write a normal Programs-and-Features entry per game (name, uninstall string, InstallLocation all correct) - only EstimatedSize is blank, because Steam owns that number, not Windows. Fixed by reading Steams own already-computed size instead of asking Windows for one it never has: Get-SteamLibrarySizes finds every Steam library via steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf (a Steam install can span multiple drives - confirmed on the operators machine, C: and D:SteamLibrary), then each librarys appmanifest_<id>.acf for installdir+SizeOnDisk, keyed by full install path. Add-GamePlatformSizes backfills sizeBytes only when the registry itself reported none and installLocation matches - nothing else about the entry is touched. Live-verified: GTA V Enhanced now reports sizeBytes=103224354965 (was blank), matching Steams own SizeOnDisk exactly. Epic support (Get-EpicManifestSizes, documented .item JSON manifest shape) implemented the same way but NOT live-tested - Epic isnt installed on the machine this was written against. Cost: lazy (only reads library/manifest files when a blank-size entry with a real install location is actually found), full-list scan measured 1209ms (up from ~350ms baseline, one-time per scan, not per-app) - not the recursive folder-size walk that cost Get-UwpApps 10-15s and was removed earlier this session. npm test 371/0, npm run verify 174/0.

Root cause was CSS, not missing error detail - the per-item error reason was already rendered (renderer.js renderPurgeSummary), but #scr-complete had no overflow-y, so .wizard-screens' overflow:hidden clipped the failures box off the bottom of the fixed-height wizard modal with no way to scroll to it. Added overflow-y:auto scoped to #scr-complete. Verified computed overflowY=auto and the failure reason text is present in the DOM via an offscreen electron harness. npm test 371/0.

Split the 'quiet' verdict on processes.length (open connections), matching design option (a)+(c): a low byte-rate sample with 0 open connections keeps the original 'Nothing on this PC is using the network' wording; a low byte-rate sample WITH open connections gets new wording ('Low traffic in this sample - not necessarily idle') that names the sample duration, the open-connection count, and states explicitly that a brief sample can miss bursty traffic - no longer conflates 'byte-rate was low' with 'nothing is using the network'. Also fixed an adjacent bug hit while verifying: rate() routed a genuine 0 B/s reading through formatBytes(0), which returns the 'Unknown' label meant for untracked sizes (same bug class as xw2) - a truly idle connection read 'Unknown/s' instead of '0 B/s'. Verified both branches via direct renderNetworkActivity calls in an offscreen electron harness. npm test 371/0. Connection-count vs byte-rate threshold logic in scanner.ps1 (Get-NetworkActivity) is unchanged - this was a display/wording fix, not an engine change.

Root cause: positionTourSpotlight's no-target branch added the 'is-hidden' class, whose CSS set opacity:0 on the spotlight element - which silently killed its own box-shadow (the mechanism that dims everything outside the spotlight's box). The comment above .tour-spotlight promised 'a plain full-screen dim' for the welcome step but the code never produced one. Fixed by keeping the spotlight visible (opacity:1, still using the same box-shadow dim as every other step) and just collapsing its box to 0x0 at viewport center, so there is no meaningful cutout but the dim still renders. Removed the now-dead, actively-wrong .is-hidden CSS rule. Verified both by computed style (opacity 1, box-shadow present) and an actual captured screenshot of the welcome step showing the background properly dimmed. npm test 371/0.

Applied position:sticky;top:0 (near-opaque + blur background matching the app's existing glass-panel look, e.g. .wizard-modal) to .apps-table th, one shared class used by all 4 actual column-header tables in the app: All Programs, Health Advisor's startup table, Task Manager, and Network Activity's process table - confirmed by grep there are no other <table><thead> instances. Verified the mechanism with getBoundingClientRect across 6 scroll positions in an offscreen electron harness: the header settles into its stuck position within the first ~100px of scroll (an 8px one-time shift from the table's own border-spacing, imperceptible) and then holds pixel-identical through scrollTop 100/300/400/700/900. npm test 371/0.

Two distinct fixes. (1) The sidebar's flexbox compression of the app list was already correct (.apps-list-container is flex:1) - the actual defect was Date/Size, short fixed-format columns, having no width floor and wrapping to two lines ('2026-' / '01-01') once compressed, reading as broken. Scoped to the All Programs sidebar specifically; Task Manager's process-details panel is untouched. Verified via geometry checks (no-selection: list gets 752 of 840px workspace width vs. previously losing 250-340px permanently; selected: Date/Size stay single-line nowrap, table does not overflow its container) and two captured screenshots in an offscreen electron harness. npm test 371/0.
